License separation

Repository code and third-party scientific articles are governed by separate licenses.

Software source code [MIT / Apache-2.0 / GPL-3.0 / OTHER] — see LICENSE
Project documentation [DOCUMENTATION LICENSE OR “same as software”]
Scientific articles Copyright remains with the respective authors or identified rightsholders. Each listed article is used under CC BY 4.0 .
Models and indexes [MODEL, EMBEDDING, OR INDEX DISTRIBUTION TERMS]

Non-endorsement and scope

Listing an author, journal, publisher, or institution does not imply endorsement, sponsorship, certification, or affiliation.

Separately credited figures, photographs, maps, tables, quotations, and supplementary files are excluded unless their reuse status is independently verified and recorded.

What this project records

Each article entry follows the Creative Commons attribution pattern of Title, Author, Source, and License, and also records the project's processing and modification history.

  • Article title and complete author attribution
  • DOI and canonical publisher source
  • CC BY 4.0 license link
  • Copyright or disclaimer notice, when supplied
  • Project use: RAG, training, evaluation, or examples
  • Text processing and modifications
  • License evidence and verification date
  • Excluded third-party material
Compact attribution format
“[ARTICLE TITLE]” by [AUTHORS], [JOURNAL] ([YEAR]), [DOI LINK]. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. Used for [PROJECT PURPOSE]. Changes: [MODIFICATIONS OR “none”].

Point-of-output attribution

When the software displays a recognizable source passage, substantial excerpt, or article-specific adaptation, place a nearby source label in addition to this registry.

Source: [FIRST AUTHOR et al., “SHORT TITLE,” JOURNAL, YEAR, DOI] — CC BY 4.0 — [modified / unmodified].

Corrections and takedown requests

Report attribution errors, license mismatches, author-name corrections, or third-party-rights concerns through [ISSUE TRACKER] or [CONTACT EMAIL].

Preserve a dated changelog for corrections and identify whether corpus files, examples, indexes, or derived artifacts were also updated.

Reference guidance

This template uses the Creative Commons TASL attribution practice and records modifications as required when changed CC BY 4.0 material is shared.
